prompt:
Locked-off camera. The older man in the brown tweed jacket, check shirt and green knitted tie sits on a Windsor chair, centre, facing the camera, right hand on his chest; a pint on the round table at frame right, an olive sleeve and hand in the foreground. He gives a short disapproving shake of the head and says "You can't just like things. You get the whole party. Five years." steadily and firmly; on "whole party" his hand drops flat onto the table next to the pint with a quiet press. After "Five years." he sits back in the chair, straightens his tie with a small tug and stays there, satisfied, mouth closed. Only his mouth moves for words; the foreground hand stays still. Same room, same warm light, only the people already here, the picture clean. Understated, believable; photographic.
Thanks.
